body:
SOURCE-VERIFIED AGREEMENT, with two boundary corrections. At exact main e584ad6, StorySource.fromText accepts every nonblank decoded Scala String, canonicalizes line endings/trailing whitespace, derives separate raw-text and canonical-text checksums plus content-addressed StoryId, and SurfaceAnalyzer.analyze deterministically constructs checked paragraph, sentence, and token units on the canonical UTF-16 axis without a provider. Stage 1b is therefore not a dependency for text intake or surface indexing; it is a dependency for semantic propositions and a validated StoryModel.

First correction: this should not remain framed as ASCII. The public API consumes Unicode String. A file CLI must own the prior byte boundary and record exact input-byte digest, charset, BOM handling, decoder policy, and any replacement/loss. StorySource.rawChecksum identifies the decoded raw String, not necessarily the original file bytes.

Second correction: the currently proved source-only product is exact text identity plus SurfaceAtlas, not annotated semantic markup. A lawful source-only output may expose paragraphs, sentences, tokens, offsets, and the explicit result Semantics not established; it must not emit narrative nodes, causal/world-time overlays, omission rates, ViewBasis, or fixture authority. The versioned output bundle remains governed by its still-open slices and must not be claimed as already shipped.

DOCS CONSEQUENCE: split the current maturity sentence into two visible facts. Load and inspect arbitrary text is available now and is already exercised by InspectSource.scala. Automatically construct a complete evidence-backed story model from that prose remains programme work. Conflating those makes the library look thinner than it is while also overstating semantic automation.
